contexts.text: From a single idea, they know of what quality he is. AC 803:2, AC 10298:5.
His quality is perceived at his first coming. AC 1383:end. AC 1388. (See AC 1520.)

The Angels regard all from their quality itself, or from their quality. The quality or quality of man, from which he is regarded in Heaven, is charity and faith. (So) when anyone regards any man, family, or nation, he thinks for the most part of what quality they are: everyone from that which then reigns with himself: the idea of their quality at once occurs, and from that he regards them in himself. Still more so the Lord; and, from Him, the Angels...
It is because there is such perception, that one can know in an instant the quality of another as to love and faith.
In Heaven they do not know Lot; but the quality represented by him.
In representations the quality of the man has no effect. Explained.
The charity with man is according to the quality and quantity of the truth. AC 2190.
Goods have their quality according to the truths and the man's life.
According to the quality and the quantity of the remains...
The quality of the Angels known from their dress.
The good itself is qualified according to the truth.
Still, the quality of good is not born and produced by truth; but by the influx of the good into truth of that quality.
According to the quality and quantity of the truth which is insinuated into good; and (then) according to the quality and quantity of the good.
Quality not predicated of the Divine; but esse.
The Lord appears to everyone according to his quality. References. AC 6832:2. HH 120. [Swedenborg footnote 2.] AE 539:4.
By quality is signified whatever is within; here, in the good of faith, and in works; and there are things innumerable; for the quality is various with everyone...
The man is then such as he had been inwardly... AC 4663:2.
Thou knowest how I have served thee () = that it knew its mind and power.
For all good has its quality from truths. AC 4197:3. AC 4301. AC 4748:2. AC 4837:2. AC 6427. AC 8768:2.
That He perceives all good as to its quality, Signified.
Their quality was known to me from their speech.
For all Spirits and Angels may be known as to their quality from the Lord's Prayer. Explained.
Charity receives its quality from the truths which are of faith.
There are degrees (of brotherhood) according to the quality of the goods and truths.
Truths are disposed according to... the quality of the good; for the good receives its quality from the truths.
All in the Grand Man keep a constant situation according to the quality and state of the truth and good in which they are, Explained.
Such as is the good, such are the truths... AC 4742:2.

When any Spirit is approaching... his presence is perceived... from a certain spiritual sphere, from which is known the quality of his life, the quality of his affection, and the quality of his faith...
That from (the Divine truth) it appeared what their quality was. Signified, Explained.
In this Light (of Heaven) all appear as to their quality. Explained [2], Example(s).
Truth does not appear as to its quality, until it is conjoined with its good. Signified.
Action itself thus qualifies truths. Explained.
But, in the other life, there is distinctly perceived both what there is in the speech and what in the action; thus the quality of the life.
By the life is not meant such as it appears in the discourse and works; but such as it is in the discourse and the works... Such as is the intention or end in (them), such is the life.
In every degree (the inflowing good) is qualified according to the reception.
From the garments of a Spirit or Angel may be Known their quality as to the truths of faith.
Hence, according to the quality of the use, is the quality of his life.
Because as yet he does not know truths, the goods of innocence and charity have not been qualified; for truths give quality to good.

Temptations give the quality of the apperception of good and truth through the opposites which are then infused. From the apperception of opposites are procured relatives, from which is all quality... AC 7319:2.
The state and quality of the spiritual life. Signified. (For) all numbers = Things; thus the state and quality of the Thing treated of.
The Divine truth which proceeds from the Lord is received by man according to his quality.
(There) such as a man had been inwardly, such he is; not such as he had appeared...
Their quality is perceived from their sphere.
The quality known from one word. AC 10454:end. (See SE 3064.)
The quality of a man's life is to be well scrutinized, and charity exercised according thereto. AC 6705.
The Lord is present according to the quality of the good.
Everyone is the neighbour according to his quality.
An angel or man is such as is his love; (and this) in the whole body.
For good to be good, there must be truths which must qualify it... therefore, such as the truth is, such becomes the good...
The quality shown by the Representative Church through truth. Signified, Explained.
That they were to be distinguished into classes according to the qualities of good. Signified.
When truth is conjoined, it qualifies the good.
The state and quality of the Law from the Divine. Signified.
From the delight may be known the quality of the love.
This good obtains its quality from truth.
Spiritual good receives its quality from the truths of faith.

The men of the Internal Church are those who have qualified their good through interior truths, such as are those of the internal sense; but the men of the External Church are those who have qualified their good through exterior truths, such as are those of the literal sense.
(These falsities) are accepted as truths according to the quality of the innocence: hence the good receives its quality.
The end is what gives quality to the actions.
The end qualifies all the other things. AC 9210. DLW 261:2.

Goods (there) are as to quality and as to quantity; (and) are defined with everyone according to the quality and quantity of his faith and charity (here). The quality and quantity of the good of everyone (there) is open before the Angels, when the Lord grants... The quality and quantity of the good possessed by everyone and by a Church, are represented by the weights and measures in the Word. Example(s).
To inflow, and thus to qualify. Signified.
The quality of spiritual good is from the truths which are of faith. The good which has not its quality from the truths of faith... is merely natural good...
The Divine appears to everyone according to the quality of him who sees it...
Love has its quality from faith.
Good has its quality from truths; and it has its form also from them; for where there is form, there is quality; and where there is not form, there is not quality. Explained.
Hence Spirits, by presence, are at once known as to their quality...
Hence Spirits and Angels, at a distance, are Known as to their quality.
For where there is quality, there is form.
Hence to number = to qualify; and, in spiritual things, the qualification of a Thing is effected through ordination and disposition by the Lord. Illustrated.
An Angel who excels in wisdom sees the quality of another instantly from his face. Explained.
Therefore the quality of all is Known in the light of Heaven...

Hence it is that the Angels know the quality of another from his speech alone; from his tone, the quality of his affection; and from the words, the quality of his mind. From a single series of the speech, the wiser Angels know the quality of the dominant affection.
Hence, according to the quality of this plane, and in such a manner as the Rational corresponds with the things there, such is the man after death.
[Swedenborg's footnote]. All good has... its quality from the uses; hence, such as is the use, such is the good. References.

After passing through the first and second states, a Spirit, when regarded with the eyes, is at once Known, as to his quality; not only from the face, but also from the body, and likewise from the speech and gestures. HH 553.
The quality of every Spirit manifests itself through influx, which is the communication of his affection. Described.

A form which does not consist of various things is not a form, because it has not quality... The quality of every form is from the ordination of the various things therein among themselves; and from their mutual regard; and from their consensus to a one...

How the Angels know the quality of a man as to understanding and will... thus as to the internal life which is of his mind, and as to the external life therefrom in the body, from the mere action of the hands. Explained.
Through the truths which are of faith, charity enters into the works, and qualifies them.
The very quality of being able to produce, earths get from their origin...
Whatever comes forth, derives from its form that which is called quality.
This is not the proprium which is meant; for it is only quality.
They do not inquire into whom and of what quality the neighbour is; because they have no truths; and by truths alone is one known from another.
That the Church may know that the Lord sees the quality of the truth and the quality of the good possessed by everyone. Signified, Explained.
Whose quality no one Knows but the Lord alone. Signified, Explained. AR 364.
Therefore there everyone knows the quality of another, as soon as he comes into his own chamber.
All quality is allotted its quality from the fact that there is an Ipsum from which it is, and to which it has relation in order to be such. Explained.
As every man, beast, bird, and fish corresponds to some quality...
Representatives of the qualities, etc., of conjugial love.
Good without something added thereto, is of no predication, of no relation, affection, or state; in a word, of no quality. It is the like with truth...
The state of man's life is his quality... as to understanding and will.
God is Form, because all the quality of substances has arisen and does arise from Him: quality exists from no other source than form.
The Truths of faith not only illuminate charity, but also qualify it.
The Lord... sees an entire society as one man; and its form from their qualities.
Who loves the person except from the quality of his will and understanding...
All the quality of good is formed through truths.
That the qualities of Spirits can be at once Known by those who are interior.
Spirits appear at a certain quarter according to their quality...
That the quality of a Spirit (or man) may be known from a single word. SE 3210. (And even from a single sigh, SE 3308.)
In like manner the evil qualities of the evil are there so much increased that...
These generals prescribe also the quality... So that there are generals of quantities and at the same time of qualities. The general of quality is the regnant one.
Everyone fares (there) according to his quality.
I know that this quality is accepted by some.
The Spiritual thinks of the quality; and the Natural of the quantity. Thus the Spiritual is not bounded...
For good puts a quality on itself through truths; for good without truths has no quality, and, where there is no quality, there there is no force or power.
To number = to know the quality of good and truth. Illustrated.
Every quality is of infinite extension...
Of what quality they are, and of what quality they have been. Signified.
When the Angels see others, they never inquire who or whence they are; but what their quality is; (for) all have habitations there according to the quality of their affections.
His quality is Known from the mere extension of his thoughts into the Societies.
5. 3. These things fall into the interior rational sight only by the abstraction or removal of quantities from qualities.
Holy Spirit. 1. 3. And [it is said] that the property and quality of the one (Person) are separate from those of another...
Trinity. 2. The idea of the wise among the clergy, is that [not] three communicable, but incommunicable, properties and qualities are meant by the three Persons.
